verdicts.not_supported: research does not back this as a general rule
verdicts.partly_true: there is something to it, but the popular version goes too far

myths.claim: Train hard in your follicular phase and go easy in your luteal phase.
myths.text: Reviews of dozens of studies found phase effects on performance are tiny and inconsistent, and no effect of phase on strength gains from training. Your own energy is a better guide than a phase rule.

myths.claim: A normal cycle is 28 days and you ovulate on day 14.
myths.text: In 600,000 cycles the average was about 29 days, and cycle length varied a lot between women and from month to month. Only about 1 in 4 women had their fertile window fully between days 10 and 17.

myths.claim: Every woman gets mood swings before her period.
myths.text: PMS affects about 20-32% of women. In a review of 47 prospective studies, many found no link between mood and cycle phase at all. Whether it happens to you is personal, and your check-ins can show it.

myths.claim: Cravings before your period mean you lack willpower.
myths.text: Appetite and cravings for chocolate, sweets and salt rise in the late luteal phase for many women, and energy use may go up a little too. It's a normal shift, not a character flaw.
